So the gap was exactly the promoted zero and nothing else. ★★ ONE GATE, THREE DOORS: C 6.5.3.3p5 makes `!E` exactly `(0 == E)` and C 6.3.1.7 makes a real→complex conversion `(the real value, +0)`; both need a float ZERO of the element type, a register machine has no float-immediate form, so the zero must be promoted to an anonymous rodata global and LOADED. `elementFloatConst` in hir_to_mir.cpp is the ONE owner of that promotion and its width list was F64/F32 only — widening it to admit F80/F128 fixes the two shapes here AND scalar `!someLongDouble` (arm 33 of examples/c/c_long_double_convert) together, and the promotion itself needed nothing new: `lowerMirGlobalsToDataItems` already widens a double-armed literal to the 80-/128-bit data item an F80/F128 global needs, which is how a source `long double g = 3.25L;` has worked since LD-1. ⚠⚠ A CLOSED ROW CLAIMS THIS ALREADY WORKED: [[D-CSUBSET-LOGICAL-NOT-ON-A-FLOAT-MINTS-A-BARE-FLOAT-CONST]] (P41) states in its trigger that "`!f`, `!d` and `!ld` compile", ✔MEASURED on pe64 — THE ONE AXIS WHERE `long double` IS `double` — so the F80/F128 arms were never exercised; that row's own FIX note is correct that F16/F80/F128 kept falling through, so its headline and its body disagreed and the headline was the false half ([[feedback-one-leg-measurement-is-a-portability-claim]]). ★ WHY A SEPARATE FILE FROM BOTH OF ITS RELATIVES, and both reasons are MEASURED rather than stylistic: NOT in `c_long_double_convert` because ✔cl.exe 19.51 refuses `__builtin_complex` outright (error C2065 — MSVC has no C99 `_Complex`) and that file's reference oracle rests on MSVC's positive vote for the f64 axis; NOT in `c99_complex_truth` because ✔a ninth arm there would need `acc += 256` and a POSIX exit status is EIGHT BITS — 511 & 0xFF is 255, which is that file's PASSING value, so the arm would have been vacuous on every Linux leg and indistinguishable from a pass (caught by running the references before trusting it). ★★ EVERY ARM IS BUILT SO THAT READING ONLY ONE COMPONENT CHANGES THE ANSWER, the same construction c99_complex_truth uses: g_imOnly=(0,7) is truthy ONLY if the imaginary part is read, and it equals g_reOnly=(5,0) ONLY if one component is ignored;
